title: Tiny Purchases Win NT$10 Million in Taiwan's Receipt Lottery
summaryZh: 統一發票開獎，10元消費也中千萬特別獎
summaryHi: ताइवान की रसीद लॉटरी में NT$10 जैसी छोटी खरीद पर भी NT$1 करोड़ का इनाम निकला।
summaryEs: En la lotería de recibos de Taiwán, compras de apenas NT$10 ganaron el premio de NT$10 millones.
summaryJa: 台湾の統一発票抽選、10元の買い物で1000万元の特別賞。
summaryKo: 대만 영수증 복권, 10대만달러 구매로 1000만 대만달러 특별상 당첨.
summaryEn: Shoppers who spent as little as NT$10 won NT$10 million in Taiwan's September–October receipt lottery.
paragraphs: Shoppers across Taiwan checked their receipts on Wednesday after the Ministry of Finance released the winning numbers for the September–October uniform invoice lottery, with major retailers soon revealing that some top prizes had gone to customers who spent only small amounts.

Taiwan's receipt lottery was created to encourage shoppers to ask for official receipts, which helps the government collect business tax. Each receipt carries an eight-digit number, and draws are held every two months. The special prize is worth NT$10 million, roughly US$300,000, while the grand prize is NT$2 million.

President Chain Store Corp., the operator of 7-Eleven, reported four special prize winners whose purchases ranged from NT$10 to NT$231. FamilyMart said two of its customers, in Nantou and Tainan, had won NT$10 million after paying just NT$46 and NT$88.
PX Mart, a supermarket chain, said one shopper in Toufen, Miaoli County, became a millionaire after buying groceries worth NT$2,244, and another in New Taipei won NT$2 million with a NT$340 purchase.
Prizes can be claimed from December 6 to March 5. Amounts up to NT$1,000 can be collected at convenience stores, while larger sums are paid at designated banks.
In Taiwan, every shop receipt has a number. Every two months, the government picks winning numbers. On Wednesday, it showed the numbers for September and October.
The top prize is NT$10 million. That is about US$300,000. Some people won it after buying very cheap things.
7-Eleven said four of its shoppers won the top prize. Some of them spent only NT$10 to NT$231. FamilyMart also had two big winners. One person paid NT$46. Another paid NT$88.
At PX Mart, one shopper in Miaoli spent NT$2,244 on food and won NT$10 million.
People can get their money from December 6 to March 5. Small prizes can be collected at a convenience store.
sentZh: 在台灣，每張商店的發票都有一個號碼。
每兩個月，政府會選出中獎號碼。
週三，政府公布了九月和十月的號碼。
最高獎金是新台幣1,000萬元。
那大約是30萬美元。
有些人買了很便宜的東西就中了這個獎。
7-Eleven說，它有四位顧客中了最高獎。
其中有些人只花了新台幣10元到231元。
全家也有兩位大獎得主。
一個人付了新台幣46元。
另一個人付了88元。
在全聯，苗栗的一位顧客花了新台幣2,244元買食物，中了1,000萬元。
大家可以從12月6日到3月5日領取獎金。
小額獎金可以在便利商店領取。

paragraphs: Taiwan's Ministry of Finance announced the winning numbers for the September–October receipt lottery on Wednesday, and several shops quickly reported that their customers had won the biggest prizes.

In Taiwan, every official shop receipt, called a uniform invoice, has an eight-digit number. The government holds a draw every two months. The special prize is NT$10 million, which is worth about US$300,000, and the grand prize is NT$2 million.

President Chain Store, which runs 7-Eleven, said four of its customers won the special prize. Their purchases cost between NT$10 and NT$231. FamilyMart had two special prize winners in Nantou and Tainan, who spent just NT$46 and NT$88.
Supermarket chain PX Mart said one shopper in Toufen, Miaoli County, won NT$10 million after buying NT$2,244 of groceries.
Winners can collect their money from December 6 until March 5 next year. Prizes of NT$1,000 or less can be picked up at convenience stores, while larger prizes are paid at certain banks.
sentZh: 財政部週三公布了九至十月統一發票的中獎號碼，幾家商店很快就宣布他們的顧客中了最大獎。
在台灣，每張正式的商店收據都叫做統一發票，上面有一組八位數號碼。
政府每兩個月舉辦一次開獎。
特別獎是新台幣1,000萬元，約合30萬美元，特獎則是新台幣200萬元。
經營7-Eleven的統一超商說，有四位顧客中了特別獎。
他們的消費金額在新台幣10元到231元之間。
全家有兩位特別獎得主，分別在南投和台南，只花了新台幣46元和88元。
連鎖超市全聯說，苗栗縣頭份的一位顧客買了新台幣2,244元的食品雜貨，中了1,000萬元。
得獎者可以從12月6日到明年3月5日領取獎金。
新台幣1,000元以下的獎金可以在便利商店領取，較高的獎金則要到指定的銀行領取。

sentZh: 財政部週三公布九至十月統一發票中獎號碼後，全台購物者紛紛核對發票，各大零售商隨即透露，有些大獎得主只花了一點點錢。

paragraphs: Receipts were scrutinised across Taiwan on Wednesday after the Ministry of Finance unveiled the winning numbers for the September–October uniform invoice lottery, and leading retailers were quick to announce that several jackpots had been claimed by customers making the most modest of purchases.

The scheme, a long-standing feature of everyday life in Taiwan, was introduced to motivate consumers to request official receipts, thereby making it harder for businesses to evade tax. Every receipt bears an eight-digit number, and draws take place bimonthly. The special prize stands at NT$10 million, approximately US$300,000, with a grand prize of NT$2 million.

President Chain Store Corp., which operates 7-Eleven, disclosed that four of its customers had scooped the special prize with purchases ranging from a mere NT$10 to NT$231. FamilyMart, meanwhile, reported two such winners in Nantou and Tainan, who had spent only NT$46 and NT$88 respectively.
At supermarket operator PX Mart, a shopper in Toufen, Miaoli County, landed NT$10 million on a NT$2,244 grocery bill.
Winnings may be collected between December 6 and March 5. Sums of up to NT$1,000 can be redeemed at convenience stores, whereas larger amounts must be claimed at designated financial institutions.
sentZh: 財政部週三揭曉九至十月統一發票中獎號碼後，全台民眾仔細檢查手上的發票，各大零售商也迅速宣布，數個頭獎都由消費金額極少的顧客抱走。
這項制度長期以來是台灣日常生活的一部分，當初推出是為了促使消費者索取正式發票，讓企業更難逃漏稅。
每張發票都印有一組八位數號碼，每兩個月開獎一次。
特別獎為新台幣1,000萬元，約30萬美元，特獎則為新台幣200萬元。
經營7-Eleven的統一超商透露，有四位顧客摘下特別獎，消費金額從區區新台幣10元到231元不等。
與此同時，全家也報告有兩位這樣的得主，分別在南投和台南，各只花了新台幣46元和88元。
在超市業者全聯，苗栗縣頭份的一位顧客以新台幣2,244元的食品帳單贏得1,000萬元。
獎金可在12月6日至3月5日之間領取。
新台幣1,000元以內的金額可在便利商店兌領，較大的金額則必須到指定的金融機構領取。

paragraphs: Consumers throughout Taiwan were examining their receipts on Wednesday after the Ministry of Finance published the winning numbers for the September–October uniform invoice lottery. Shortly afterwards, major retailers announced that a number of the largest prizes had been won by customers whose purchases were remarkably inexpensive.

The lottery was established with a clear fiscal objective: to give consumers an incentive to obtain official receipts, which in turn makes it considerably more difficult for businesses to under-report their sales and avoid taxation. Each receipt displays an eight-digit number, and a draw is held every two months. The special prize amounts to NT$10 million, equivalent to roughly US$300,000, while the grand prize is NT$2 million.

President Chain Store Corp., the operator of 7-Eleven, stated that four of its customers had secured the special prize with transactions ranging from NT$10 to NT$231. Similarly, FamilyMart indicated that two winners, in Nantou and Tainan, had paid merely NT$46 and NT$88.
Meanwhile, PX Mart reported that a shopper in Toufen, Miaoli County, had obtained the top prize after a grocery purchase of NT$2,244.
The claim period runs from December 6 until March 5. Prizes not exceeding NT$1,000 may be collected at convenience stores, whereas larger sums are distributed through designated banks.
sentZh: 財政部週三公布九至十月統一發票的中獎號碼後，全台消費者都在檢查自己的發票。
不久之後，各大零售商宣布，多個最大獎項是由消費金額格外低廉的顧客贏得。
這項抽獎制度的設立有明確的財政目標：給消費者索取正式發票的誘因，進而讓企業更難短報營業額和逃稅。
每張發票都印有一組八位數號碼，每兩個月開獎一次。
特別獎金額為新台幣1,000萬元，相當於約30萬美元，特獎則為新台幣200萬元。
經營7-Eleven的統一超商表示，有四位顧客以新台幣10元到231元不等的交易獲得特別獎。
同樣地，全家指出，有兩位分別在南投和台南的得主，只付了新台幣46元和88元。
與此同時，全聯報告，苗栗縣頭份的一位顧客在購買了新台幣2,244元的食品雜貨後獲得最高獎。
領獎期間從12月6日至3月5日。
不超過新台幣1,000元的獎金可在便利商店領取，較大的金額則透過指定銀行發放。

note.meaning: 目標（名詞）；客觀的（形容詞）。
note.usage: 名詞：achieve/meet an objective；形容詞 objective 意為「客觀的」。

example.en: The main objective is to cut waste by half.
example.zh: 主要目標是把浪費減半。

noteHi.usage: achieve an objective; विशेषण के रूप में "वस्तुनिष्ठ"।
noteHi.exampleTr: मुख्य उद्देश्य बर्बादी को आधा करना है।

noteEs.usage: achieve an objective; como adjetivo significa «objetivo, imparcial».
noteEs.exampleTr: El objetivo principal es reducir el desperdicio a la mitad.

noteJa.meaning: 目的、目標（形容詞では「客観的な」）。
noteJa.exampleTr: 主な目的は無駄を半分に減らすことだ。

noteKo.exampleTr: 주요 목표는 낭비를 절반으로 줄이는 것이다.

noteEn.meaning: a goal you are trying to achieve.
noteEn.usage: Noun: 'achieve an objective'; as an adjective it means 'not biased'.

obtain.ex: You must obtain a permit first.

obtained.ex: Reporters obtained a copy of the letter.

official.en: approved by the government or an authority
official.ex: Ask the shop for an official receipt.

on.ex: Voting will go on for nine days.

only.ex: The museum is only open on weekends.

operator.en: a company that runs a business or service
operator.ex: The tour operator cancelled all trips to the island.

paid.ex: The trip was paid for by the school.

paying.ex: Tenants paying high rents need help.

period.ex: Prices fell over a short period.

picked.ex: Your parcel can be picked up at the store.

picks.ex: He always picks the red one.

place.ex: The draw takes place on the 25th.

president.zh: 統一（President Chain Store：統一超商）
president.en: part of a company name (President Chain Store)

prize.en: an award given to a winner
prize.ex: She won a prize for her short story.

prizes.ex: Two more farmers also got prizes.

published.ex: The report was published on Monday.

purchase.ex: The purchase of the land was finally agreed.

purchases.ex: Online purchases rose sharply last year.

px.en: part of a shop name (PX Mart)

quick.ex: She was quick to thank her team.

ranging.en: covering a range between two points
ranging.ex: We sell shoes ranging from small to very large.

receipt.en: a paper showing what you bought and paid
receipt.ex: Keep the receipt in case you return it.

receipts.en: papers showing what you bought and paid
receipts.ex: Keep all your receipts in a box.

redeemed.ex: Points can be redeemed for flights.

note.usage: 修飾形容詞：remarkably cheap/similar；表示令人驚訝的程度。

example.en: The old phone still works remarkably well.
example.zh: 這支舊手機仍然出奇地好用。

noteHi.meaning: उल्लेखनीय रूप से; आश्चर्यजनक रूप से।
noteHi.exampleTr: पुराना फ़ोन अब भी उल्लेखनीय रूप से अच्छा काम करता है।

noteEs.exampleTr: El teléfono viejo sigue funcionando notablemente bien.

noteJa.exampleTr: 古い電話はいまだに驚くほどよく動く。

noteKo.exampleTr: 오래된 휴대폰이 여전히 놀라울 정도로 잘 작동한다.

reported.ex: Half of students reported feeling stressed.

request.en: the act of asking for something

respectively.en: in the same order as just mentioned
respectively.ex: Tom and Ann are 10 and 12 respectively.

retailers.en: shops or companies that sell goods to people
retailers.ex: Many retailers offer discounts in January.

revealing.ex: The photo revealed a hidden door.

runs.en: manages a business; continues for a period
runs.ex: The festival runs from May to June.

said.ex: She said the bus was late again.

scheme.ex: The scheme will connect two towns.

scooped.en: won a prize, often against others
scooped.ex: The band scooped three music awards.

scrutinised.ex: Every line of the contract was scrutinised by lawyers.

example.en: The plan will be scrutinised by experts.
example.zh: 該計畫將由專家仔細審查。

note.usage: scrutinise a bill/proposal；英式拼法 -ise，美式 -ize。

noteHi.exampleTr: योजना की विशेषज्ञ बारीकी से जाँच करेंगे।

noteEs.exampleTr: El plan será examinado por expertos.

noteJa.exampleTr: その計画は専門家によって精査される。
noteJa.usage: scrutinise a bill/proposal の形。英綴り -ise。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 계획은 전문가들이 면밀히 검토할 것이다.
noteKo.usage: scrutinise a bill/proposal 형태. 영국식 철자 -ise.

shop.ex: She runs a small shop in the village.

shopper.en: a person who is buying things
shopper.ex: One lucky shopper won a free trip.

shoppers.en: people who buy things in shops
shoppers.ex: The mall was full of shoppers on Saturday.

shops.ex: The local shop closes at nine.

showed.ex: The report showed a big rise in prices.

similarly.ex: Prices rose, and wages rose similarly.

small.ex: They live in a small house by the sea.

some.en: a number of, but not all

soon.ex: Soon after, it began to rain.

special.en: different and given for a reason
special.ex: He got a special prize for effort.

spent.en: used money to pay for something
spent.ex: They have spent their savings on a new car.
spent.zh: 花費了（spend 的過去分詞）

stands.en: is at a particular amount (stands at)
stands.ex: The price now stands at NT$50.

stated.ex: The letter stated that he had been fired.

store.en: a shop; to keep things for later
store.ex: The new store opens next week.

sums.ex: Large sums were spent on roads.

supermarket.ex: I buy milk at the supermarket.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

take.ex: The meeting will take place tomorrow.

tax.ex: The government plans a new tax on sugar.

taxation.ex: Fair taxation is important for public services.

thereby.ex: He sold his car, thereby saving money.

things.ex: We packed a few things for the trip.

through.ex: They bought it through a special deal.

throughout.ex: The festival is popular throughout Taiwan.

toufen.en: a city in Miaoli County, Taiwan

transactions.en: business deals of buying and selling
transactions.ex: All card transactions are recorded by the bank.

turn.ex: Better sleep, in turn, helps you study.

under-report.en: to report a smaller amount than the true one

uniform.ex: All forms must follow a uniform style.

unveiled.en: shown to the public for the first time
unveiled.ex: A new statue was unveiled today.

was.ex: The shop was open every day.

were.ex: The shops were closed on Sunday.

who.en: used to add information about a person

winners.ex: The winners will get a prize.

winning.ex: The film left with two awards, winning Best Screenplay.

winnings.ex: She gave half her winnings to charity.

won.ex: Our team won the cup last year.

year.ex: The festival happens once a year.
